problem: Customers had little chance to see and try Apple products in a good setting.
title: Apple opens its own retail stores despite predictions they would fail
context: Apple sold its computers mainly through third-party retailers.
decision_made: Open Apple-owned retail stores, with 25 planned in 2001.
action_taken: The first two stores opened on 19 May 2001 at Tysons Corner, Virginia and Glendale, California.
observed_outcome: Critics such as BusinessWeek said the stores would not work. Apple later operated about 534 stores in 27 countries, and Fortune called the decision the right one by a wide margin.
lessons: Skeptical press predictions about a retail strategy are not strong evidence, and control of the customer experience can be valuable.
limitations: The later success depended on Apple's products such as the iPhone, so the stores' effect alone is hard to isolate. The BusinessWeek piece was known only through secondary quotes.

claims.claim_text: Apple announced 25 retail stores for 2001, with the first two opening on 19 May.
Fortune's 2011 retrospective described the store decision as right and recalled the skeptical press coverage in 2001.
